editorial.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has gathered a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers, and AWS's SageMaker guide.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 27: CoHARL co-trains agent policies with their executable harnesses, and EnvSched schedules environments under a fixed rollout budget; both are arXiv papers.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent RL is now judged on cost and reliability: EnvSched and calibrated budgets (Oct 20) target rollout spend, while MiRL and CalibraRL target named failures. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, measure rollout cost per environment (EnvSched, calibrated budgets), log recurring failure modes for error-targeted RL (MiRL), and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat paper results as unreplicated until rerun on your own evals.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest aim at harness co-training, rollout cost, agent reliability and credit-assignment limits.

open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does Qwen publish QwenGyre weights, code, or benchmarks that show the elastic RL gain on long-horizon agent tasks?
Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
Does twin-world credit assignment improve agent training on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Do MiRL's error-targeted fixes hold on terminal-agent tasks outside the paper's own benchmark?
Does EnvSched's scheduling gain hold on agent-RL benchmarks beyond the paper's own, and with which environment mixes?
